DCAF organised the Second Workshop on Conceptualising Procedures for Destroying Data Produced by Special Investigative Measures (SIM) in September 2023. This workshop continued work towards the development of a procedure on data destruction to safeguard citizens’ privacy. Future workshops organised by DCAF will result in the approval of the procedure.

title.narrative: Indicator #1.1.1: DCAF recommendation, including on gender and human rights obligations, taken into consideration as part of the legislative review process.

comment.narrative: Current laws do not foster effective oversight. Enhanced legal authority and access to information are required to make oversight effective, in the Macedonian political context. The current law on AR, from 1996, does not sufficiently address increased requirements for intelligence accountability nor the new intelligence sector landscape, with OTA and the new law on intelligence coordination. No law on parliamentary oversight of intelligence exists, allowing for clear oversight powers, roles and effective oversight.
By 2025 DCAF has provided recommendations respond to real gaps in law and real problems in implementation.

DCAF provided recommendations on the revision of LIC that was adopted in July 2023. The revision responded to existing gaps in the law and will make the Council for Civilian Supervision better able to function.

title.narrative: Indicator #2.8.2 : Employees in the Section for Internal Control, Criminal Investigations and Professional Standards receive training for the purpose of implementing the Integrity Test (use of audio and video equipment for simulated situations).

comment.narrative: Over the last two years DCAF supported the MoI in the development and drafting of the Integrity Plan. Presently, the Integrity Plan is pending approval from the Minister of Interior. The Ministry of Interior (MoI) is amending the law on internal affairs to improve the internal control mechanisms that promote integrity. The new law will include integrity testing measures as a means of internal control, which will be applied to both current and future employees of the MoI. The MoI does not possess technical equipment to perform professional integrity testing, which will be a requirement in accordance to the new Law on Internal Affairs. In addition, the North Macedonian Police have revised their Code of Ethics in 2020.
By 2022 all employees in the SICPS received training on integrity testing.

DCAF organised a working visit for representatives of the internal control department of the Macedonian MoI to the Serbian MoI on the subject of integrity testing. This practical exchange of experiences allowed Macedonian MoI representatives to increase their understanding of possible integrity testing scenarios which will contribute to their ability to design and implement their own tests.

title.narrative: Indicator #1.5.1: Relevant experts from the Ministry of Interior, and other relevant institutions if necessary, are actively engaged in the drafting of normative/legal documents (e.g. regulations, amendments to national laws or by-laws).

comment.narrative: Some normative/legal capacities are already in place. Some of these existing documents will require amendments, while some additional documents might need to be created.
a. By the end of 2022, the necessary normative/legal documents drafted and assessed by selected experts from EU Member States.b. By mid-2023, the normative/legal documents adopted.

In this period, DCAF organised two workshops on Revising the Interpretation Guideline for Autosomal STR (Short Tandem Repeat) Profiling for a working group from the Forensics Department of the MoI. The working group revised and improved the profiling guidelines, reporting approaches, and methods for interpreting DNA profiles after genotyping. The guidelines were then reviewed by other representatives of the Department. The review was led by the Head of the Unit and discussions centred around best practices and international recommendations and standards on STR profiling, including PCC Prüm requirements related to the storage, processing, and automated exchange of DNA data. DCAF will continue to support the Forensics Department to improve its internal procedures related to DNA data sampling, processing, profiling analysis, interpretation, and exchange. The Guideline is expected to be completed in the next two months, subject to approval and adoption by the MoI.

title.narrative: Indicator #2.2 a: Increased consistency of judicial practice (prosecutors and judges) in authorization and review of intrusive methods (intrusive methods to be based on law, be non-discriminatory, have a legitimate aim, and be a “necessary” and “proportional” response).

comment.narrative: The ECHR case law is not regularly observed by prosecutors and judges in the request and authorisation of intrusive methods. The judicial practice (interpretation and application of law by prosecutors and judges) in authorization of intrusive methods is still not consistent and adequate.
By 2025 judicial practice in authorisation of intrusive methods is more consistent and adequate compared to 2020.

On 4 July 2023, DCAF organised a Workshop on Developing Methodology for Case-Law Collection on SIMs. A team of three legal advisors from the Basic Criminal Court and Basic Public Prosecution Office and a criminal law professor (the editor of the Collection) agreed on a methodology for developing the Collection of Case-Law on Special Investigative Measures (SIM) in North Macedonia. The team is currently working on identifying cases and extracting relevant information from those selected to compile the Collection. The Collection will serve as a training resource for the Academy for Judges and Public Prosecutors and is expected to be used in judicial courses at both entry- and higher-level education. This Collection will complement the Judicial Benchbook, previously developed with DCAF’s support, and facilitate its application to local practice. The Collection will ensure that standards of the European Convention on Human Rights are applied to SIM authorisation in Macedonian proceedings and judicial reasoning.

title.narrative: Indicator #2.3.1: Shielded Room and protected workspace constructed in Parliament and equipment installed.

comment.narrative: The Parliament has no protected workspace and meeting facility to discuss and store classified information, impeding meaningful exchange of sensitive and classified information with security and intelligence services. Parliament, in Feb 2020, approved the establishment of the shielded room. Within its Phase I Programme DCAF allocated funds as a contribution towards the establishment of the Shielded Room and protected workplace. Due to Covid-19 the process was delayed throughout 2020.

The construction, directed by Parliament and supported by DCAF, commenced in July 2023. In addition, DCAF continues to facilitate the process of producing accreditation documents for the use of the Shielded Room.

title.narrative: Indicator #2.3: The Ministry of Interior of North Macedonia (MoI) has strategic and operational capacity to effectively build integrity in line with European values and good policing practice, enabling more effective oversight.

comment.narrative: The Section for Internal Control, Criminal Investigations, and Professional Standards (SICPS), in cooperation with DCAF, developed an Integrity Plan over the past three years. The Plan assesses the corruption risk of all job positions in the Ministry of Interior, in accordance with the Rulebook on systematization of job positions in the MoI, proposing measures aimed to reduce risk.
By end of the programme the MoI (SICPS) is successfully implementing the Integrity Plan

DCAF organised a Meeting of the Working Group (WG) for Developing a Curricula for Training Courses on Police Integrity on 15 September 2023. The WG is comprised of representatives of the Department for Internal Control, Criminal Investigations, and Professional Standards and the Police Training Centre and is supported by DCAF and trainers from the MoI participating in an OSCE project focused on hybrid training. During the meeting, the WG developed curricula for conducting training courses for police officers in different organisational units of the MoI identified as most vulnerable to corruption. The curricula has been submitted to the Minister of Interior for approval. The presence of integrity training curricula will allow the trainings planned in the Integrity Plan to be implemented in a sustainable and uniform way.

title.narrative: Indicator #1.1 a Amended laws, bi-laws and procedures on intelligence aligned with international principles, gender and human rights obligations, good practice and respecting the diversity of the citizens of the Republic of North Macedonia, adopted by Parliament.

comment.narrative: The current law, by-laws and procedures are not suitable to allow for effective oversight of the intelligence services. In addition, legally mandated oversight bodies are functioning but not sufficiently effective. The formal relationship between the Parliament and the Council for Civilian Supervision remains inadequate as a result.
By 2023 North Macedonia has suitable laws, by-laws and procedures (Law on Interception of Communications and other relevant laws;) allowing effective oversight over the intelligence services.

On 18 July 2023, the Parliament of North Macedonia passed the amendment of the Law on Interception of Communications (LIC) with a 2/3 majority (80 votes in favour). The adoption of the LIC amendment provides a legal basis for the proper functioning of the Council for Civilian Supervision (CCS) and Parliament’s engagement of technical experts to support the Council. DCAF facilitated the amendment process, contributing to the law’s text and assisting to achieve political consensus.

title.narrative: Indicator 2.11.1 Recommendations from the Gender Self-Assessment are translated into a Gender Action Plan by the Ministry of Defense.

comment.narrative: Within the Ministry of Defence (MoD), despite of the existing gender-sensitive policies, which have so far made significant progress in terms of gender responsiveness of the institution, there is still no evidence-based research on the degree of progress in enhancing gender-responsive practices, as well as on the potential gaps and weaknesses in the domain of the gender mainstreaming.
By 2025, a Gender Action Plan is developed for the Ministry of Defense and the Army.

DCAF proceeded with activities that are part of the Gender Self-Assessment (GSA) process in the Ministry of Defence (MoD) and the Army of North Macedonia. The field research that began in May 2023 was finalised at the end September 2023. The field research consisted of interviews with key leaders from the MoD and the Army, focus groups with MoD and Army personnel, and surveys conducted with a representative sample of the MoD and Army staff. A series of focus groups with MoD and Army personnel focused on different subject matters related to gender mainstreaming were conducted in various barracks in North Macedonia. The survey (consisting of closed and open-ended questions) was disseminated both online and with hard copies throughout different military units. In the next period, the data collected will be analysed by experts with contribution from the MoD’s Working Group (WG), to identify gaps and weaknesses in the MoD and Army’s structures regarding gender equality as well as opportunities and entry points for gender mainstreaming.

title.narrative: Quarterly Report October - December 2023
Newsletter No. 10: October - December 2023
Indicator #2.1.2: Oversight actors feel more confident in institutional cooperation and exchange .

comment.narrative: Baseline #2.1.1 – 2.1.2: Insufficient cooperation between intelligence/security services and legally mandated oversight actors.
By end of 2023 80% of the actors expressed feeling more confident in institutional cooperation and exchange.

During this period, DCAF engaged with the ombuds institution to increase its confidence for performing oversight activities.From 26 to 27 October, DCAF organised the first training for representatives of the Ombuds institution in North Macedonia entitled: "The Oversight Role of the Ombudsman over Intelligence and Security". The objective of the training was to familiarise the representatives of the Ombuds institution in North Macedonia with oversight principles, the institutions’ responsibilities for oversight, and the role of Ombuds institutions in enhancing security sector reform. The training utilised expert sessions on theory, practical exercises, and case studies to encourage a discussion of existing challenges to performing effective oversight. DCAF will continue to support the representatives of the Ombuds institution to strengthen their oversight role in the intelligence and security sector. On 8 November, DCAF, in cooperation with the Ombudsperson of North Macedonia, organised a “Conference on the Oversight Role of the Ombudsperson over Intelligence and Security” in Skopje.The event featured a wide range of prominent speakers, panelists, and over 100 attendees. Among the key speakers of the event were the President of North Macedonia and DCAF’s Assistant Director, Mr. Hans Born. During the conference, speakers and panelists examined the possibility of strengthening the Ombudsperson's role as an oversight actor in the intelligence and security sector and exchanged European practices for Ombuds institutions in intelligence and security sector oversight. The event convened a diverse range of participants including Members of Parliament, representatives of the Government, employees of the Ombudsperson office in North Macedonia, security institutions, and intelligence agencies, independent experts, the academic community, civil society, media, as well as senior representatives of the international community in North Macedonia.
By end of 2023 80% of the actors expressed feeling more confident in institutional cooperation and exchange.

During this period, DCAF worked with parts of the intelligence community on increasing their reporting capacities, transparency policies, and use of good governance. These activities contribute to improve the confidence of oversight actors by improving inter-institutional cooperation and exchange.DCAF organised a Workshop on Reporting and Inter-Institutional Cooperation in Skopje on 17 October and Workshop on Intelligence Budgeting and Management of Special Funds in Ljubljana between 05-07 December for senior-level managers in the intelligence institutions. During the first workshop, participants discussed tools for reporting to the public and respective institutions, reporting standards, and mechanisms for inter-institutional cooperation. During the second workshop, participants discussed budgeting, such as the intelligence budget cycle as a process through which funds (budgets) for the operation of intelligence services are formed, approved, implemented (spent), and reviewed (controlled). DCAF’s expert additionally facilitated a discussion around the role of public finance principles and intelligence tasking in guiding the formation of intelligence budgets facilitated.Between 6 and 10 November, DCAF organised a Training of Trainers (ToT) Course for the Military Service for Security and Intelligence (MSSI) in Berovo, North Macedonia. The course focused on increasing participants’ knowledge of learning and teaching methods and principles and bringing education and training closer to operational needs to enhance the training system in the MSSI. The participants of the ToT will be able to apply their knowledge by delivering courses on military intelligence and good governance organised by the MSSI and DCAF in December 2023 and January 2024.Subsequently, between 11 and 22 December in Skopje, DCAF and the MSSI organised the first Course for Military Security and Intelligence and Good Governance. The course contains material on good governance in the security sector with a focus on military security and intelligence. The first course was attended by sixteen participants at the mid-management level and increased levels of understanding of the importance of applying democratic and good governance standards in security institutions and the influence of good governance on the professionalism, productivity, transparency, and accountability of the security sector.

title.narrative: Indicator #3.1.1: CSOs and Media report improved understanding of intelligence sector reforms, accountability requirements and police integrity

comment.narrative: CSOs and Media are not sufficiently equipped with knowledge and skills on intelligence sector reforms and accountability requirements, and police integrity to do monitoring and assessments of intelligence and security sector reforms.
By 2023, 5 trainings/workshops delivered to CSOs and Media.

During this period, much progress was made on training representatives of CSOs and media and facilitating an exchange between state and non-state actors. Between 18 and 20 October 2023, DCAF organised a Multi-Stakeholder Workshop entitled “Reconciling security sector and justice sector reform in North Macedonia” in Mavrovo. The workshop brought together representatives from local CSOs/media, Parliament (MPs and staff) and the Judiciary (judges and public prosecutors) with the aim to increase their understanding of each stakeholders’ roles and responsibilities in ensuring effective and accountable intelligence and security sector governance.Through tailor-made exercises and a scenario-based simulation, participants had the opportunity to enhance their knowledge on different forms of oversight in line with international human rights standards. In addition, the workshop served as a platform for building trust and cooperation between different oversight actors through their joint definition of the functions and challenges of the intelligence and security sector.The workshop "Developing Standardised Guidelines for Civilian Oversight of Intelligence and Security by Civil Organisations and the Media" was organised between 23 and 25 November in Strumica and attended by representatives of CSOs, the media, and Parliament. This workshop was designed to encourage participants to contribute to the development of common standardised guidelines for effective civilian oversight over intelligence and security. The workshop included dynamic plenary discussions and breakout sessions moderated by an expert.Subsequently, on 15 December 2023, DCAF organised a Workshop for the Validation of the Standardised Guidelines for Civilian Oversight of Intelligence and Security by CSOs and Media in North Macedonia.The workshop also marked the conclusion of the first phase of a year-long capacity-building process on "Security Sector Governance and Accountability" that was designed for CSO and media representatives in North Macedonia.These guidelines are designed to serve as a structural framework, outlining principles, standards, and norms for civilian oversight of the intelligence and security sector that were defined by CSO and media representatives in North Macedonia. The guidelines are a practical resource and should assist the CSOs and media to methodically and systematically engage in democratic oversight of intelligence and security sector institutions in North Macedonia.
By 2023, 5 trainings/workshops delivered to CSOs and Media.

To increase the exchange between the security sector/intelligence institutions and CSOs and media outlets on gender equality in terms of SSR, DCAF organised a Gender Talk on 21 December 2023. The event was on the topic of Gender Perspectives of the Intelligence Sector in cooperation with UNI-FORM (Association of Women from the Security Sector). The Gender Talks are moderated discussions aimed to prompt reflections on progress and challenges of gender mainstreaming practices in intelligence and security institutions in North Macedonia. The first Gender Talk featured speakers from the Intelligence Agency and the Operational-Technical Agency (OTA) who explained their institutions’ approach to gender mainstreaming.The audience consisted of representatives of intelligence and security institutions, CSOs, the media, and the academic community. The event garnered great interest and prompted interesting discussions.

title.narrative: Indicator #1.4.2: Inter-institutional Protocols, harmonised Templates and Guidelines for different stages of SIM approval are drafted and submitted for approval by relevant institutions within the criminal justice chain.

comment.narrative: Courts and prosecutorial offices have different (sometimes dated, or even contradictory) procedures and templates used in the authorisation of SIM. Harmonisation of practice and exchange of information are not in place to ensure effective authorisation of SIM, in agreement with new legislative provisions and European standards.
By 2022 working groups draft proposals designed to unify and harmonise practice.

At the request of the Criminal Court in Skopje, DCAF organised a Third Workshop on Conceptualising Procedures for Destroying Data Produced by Special Investigative Measures (SIM) from November 29 to December 01 in Popova Shapka. This workshop addressed the need for a specific procedure for the destruction of data produced by SIM, recognised over the past two years during DCAF's multistakeholder workshops on measures for the interception of communications. The Agency for Personal Data Protection recommended the development of this procedure to protect citizens' privacy. Engaging representatives from various institutions, specifically the Judiciary (Supreme Court, Basic Criminal Court, Basic Public Prosecution Skopje, Basic Public Prosecution for Organised Crime and Corruption), Ministry of Interior, Ministry of Justice, Agency for Personal Data Protection, Directorate for Security of Classified Information, State Archive, Lawyer Chamber, and academia, the workshop focused on drafting procedures for the destruction of SIM-generated data. Discussions covered legal basis, responsible parties, steps, and deadlines for data retention and destruction. Following the workshop, the Guidelines for the Destruction of Data Produced by SIMs were presented in a coordination meeting held in Skopje on 21 December. The Ministry of Justice is presently distributing the Guidelines to stakeholders for feedback and DCAF will continue supporting the institutions for its finalisation. Upon finalisation, legal practitioners will initiate the implementation of the Guidelines, starting with a pilot phase in judicial institutions nationwide.

title.narrative: Indicator #2.9.1: Selected employees from the Ministry of Interior successfully conclude vocational trainings.

comment.narrative: Employees from the Ministry of Interior, e.g. the Section for Crime – Technical Analysis and Expertise, and the National Central Unit for Information Exchange, are not sufficiently equipped with knowledge to administer automated exchange of DNA data.

DCAF organised a Workshop on Revising the Guidelines and Strategy for Recovering Biological Samples for DNA Analysis in Skopje from 6 to 8 November. The purpose of the workshop, facilitated by an international expert in forensic science and DNA analysis, was to allow members of the Laboratory for the Reception and Selection of Biological Material to review comments, advice, and suggestions for improving the Guidelines developed by the expert. The Guidelines explain the entire process of forensic-technical processing and are intended to reduce the risks of cross-contamination, or complete destruction, of traces of biological origin while ensuring uniformity in the processing of biological traces for DNA analysis. Once completed and internally approved, the Laboratory representatives will consult the Guidelines during their work in order to enhance the quality of collected traces.

title.narrative: Indicator #2.6.1: A system for accountability in the use of intrusive methods (SIM), where different actors involved are aware of each other’s role and function in complementarity (judiciary, parliamentary committees, law enforcement, CCS, etc) is developed.

The training was delivered by a team of four senior experts from EU countries, specifically Austria, Croatia, Slovenia, and Finland, who shared their extensive knowledge of European jurisprudence and rich practical experience in criminal investigations and the implementation of SIMs. This unique training exposed participants to specialised knowledge and expertise, emphasising the value of enriching participants’ understanding of international standards and practices in judicial control.

These multi-stakeholder gatherings provide unique opportunity for networking, exchange of experiences and trust building between different oversight actors.

A Hybrid Workshop on "Y-STR – Procedures and Guidelines for the Interpretation and Evaluation of Y-STR Results" was held in Skopje from November 14 to 15. This workshop aimed to describe the method for evaluating and interpreting DNA profiles when determining Y chromosome haplotypes, as well as the phraseological interpretation of these results. This applies to profiles obtained through work in the DNA identification laboratory or those forwarded by another institution. Once finalized and internally approved, laboratory representatives will refer to these guidelines during their work to improve the quality of collected trace evidence.
By the end of 2023, relevant employees from the Ministry of Interior received the necessary vocational trainings.

DCAF organized a workshop on "Guidelines for the Interpretation and Evaluation of Kinship Analysis – Missing Persons, Unidentified Human Remains, and Crime Traces" in Skopje, held from October 8 to 9. The purpose of these guidelines is to outline the process for interpreting the results of familial and kinship connections during the analysis and comparison of DNA profiles. This includes profiles obtained at the DNA Laboratory of Reference Biological Material in the Registration Department, as well as those received from other institutions, both domestically and internationally. The guidelines provide a comprehensive explanation of the forensic-technical processing steps and aim to ensure accurate interpretation of kinship analysis for missing persons, unidentified human remains, and crime trace evidence.

title.narrative: Indicator #2.8.1: DICCIPS’ employees have updated knowledge and skills to perform their duties related to preventing corruption and integrity violations more efficiently within the MoI.

comment.narrative: Over the last two years DCAF supported the MoI in the development and drafting of the Integrity Plan. Presently, the Integrity Plan is pending approval from the Minister of Interior. The Ministry of Interior (MoI) is amending the law on internal affairs to improve the internal control mechanisms that promote integrity. The new law will include integrity testing measures as a means of internal control, which will be applied to both current and future employees of the MoI. The MoI does not possess technical equipment to perform professional integrity testing, which will be a requirement in accordance to the new Law on Internal Affairs. In addition, the North Macedonian Police have revised their Code of Ethics in 2020.
By the end of 2025, 80% of DICCIPS employees report increasing their capacities for conducting criminal and disciplinary investigations.

DCAF organised two Training Courses on Criminal Investigations for Crimes Committed by Police Officers in Berovo from 17 to 19 October and in Ohrid from 31 October to 02 November. The trainings engaged two groups of 20 participants from the Department for Internal Control, Criminal Investigations, and Professional Standards and responded to the MoI’s need for strengthened capacities for conducting criminal investigations in line with the Law on Internal Affairs. Facilitated by judicial practitioners (three public prosecutors, two judges, and a defence lawyer), the training aimed to increase participants’ knowledge on conducting investigations and collecting evidence as well as enhance cooperation, communication, and coordination between the Department and the public prosecution and courts. Participants engaged in discussions with the experts, shared experiences, identified key challenges and gaps in communication and coordination with the judiciary, and proposed potential solutions for increasing the effectiveness and efficiency of criminal investigations. DCAF remains committed to support the Department for Internal Control, Criminal Investigations and Professional Standards to increase its investigative capacities and cooperation and coordination with the Department for Disciplinary Proceedings and Prosecutors Office.
By the end of 2025, 80% of DICCIPS employees report increasing their capacities for conducting criminal and disciplinary investigations.

DCAF supported the participation of the representatives of the MoI Department for Internal Control, Criminal Investigations and Professional Standards (DICCIPS) at the Regional Anti-Corruption Conference “Building Integrity from Within: Strengthening Internal Control for a Corruption-Free Future”, from 3 to 4 December 2024, in Chisinau Moldova. The conference brought representatives of security sector institutions from across Europe, including representatives from Ukraine, Estonia, Lithuania, Poland, Serbia, Romania, and North Macedonia, to exchange best practice on internal control mechanisms in law enforcement. The conference featured panels on the role of internal control units in national anti-corruption strategies, challenges and opportunities in building institutional integrity, regional cooperation on anti-corruption efforts, and emerging corruption threats and future trends. DCAF will continue to support regional efforts to enhance anti-corruption measures and promote integrity within security sector institutions.

title.narrative: Indicator #2.1.3: Gender Action Plan developed by MoD based on recommendations in the Gender-Self Assessment report and MoD increases its capacity to implement the Plan.

comment.narrative: The MoD does not currently have a specific, evidence-based gender action plan aimed at enhancing gender equality in the institution based on an in-depth institutional gender analysis.
By the end of 2025, relevant staff have developed capacities to implement and monitor the Gender Action Plan.

DCAF continued to support the development of the Gender Action Plan in the Ministry of Defence (MoD) and the Army. On 9 October 2024, representatives from DCAF’s Skopje office met with the Minister of Defense of North Macedonia, Mr Vlado Misajlovski. Discussion focused on ongoing processes within the MoD, supported through the DCAF’s Intelligence and Security Sector Reform Programme in North Macedonia, including the gender self-assessment process and the capacity building process of the Military Service for Security and Intelligence (MSSI). The meeting also emphasized DCAF's support to furthering gender equality in the defence through implementation of the Gender Action Plan (2024-2028) in the MoD and the Army of North Macedonia. Both Minister Misajlovski and the DCAF representatives reaffirmed the importance of continuing the reform processes and expressed their commitment to further strengthening their cooperation. They emphasized the value of sustained collaboration in advancing key reforms within the security sector.
By the end of 2025, relevant staff have developed capacities to implement and monitor the Gender Action Plan.

Following the Gender Self-Assessment process, the Ministry of Defense (MoD) took a significant step towards advancing gender equality by establishing a working group to implement the Gender Action Plan (2024–2028). To support this effort, DCAF, in collaboration with the Dutch Royal Army, organized a Working Visit to the Netherlands which took place between 10-13 December 2024. This visit offered Macedonian MoD and Army personnel a unique opportunity to learn from the Dutch Royal Army’s successful integration of gender perspectives into military operations and organizational culture. The program provided practical insights, best practices, and firsthand experiences and approaches to gender mainstreaming within the defence sector, which could be adapted to fit the Macedonian context. The Netherlands is widely regarded as a leader in this field, having successfully implemented its Defence Action Plan and demonstrated a strong commitment to embedding gender perspectives across all levels of its military sector. The working visit provided meaningful exchanges on institutional mechanisms, leadership engagement, and gender-responsive policies. DCAF will continue to support the MoD through the implementation process through capacity-building initiatives and expert guidance.

title.narrative: Indicator #2.2.6: The targeted staff at the Ombudsperson institution have a better understanding of their role as oversight actors.

comment.narrative: The Ombudsperson institution, although legally mandated for oversight over intelligence and security, still has no capacities to conduct proper oversight.
By the end of 2025, at least 8 staff members of the Ombudsperson institution report improved practical and theoretical knowledge on how to conduct oversight over intelligence and security.

Between 16-17 December 2024, “Workshop on Strengthening Capacities for Independent Oversight of the Ombudsperson of North Macedonia” was organized. The workshop contained ability self-assessment session which allowed participants to evaluate their institutional strengths and areas for improvement. A moderated discussion focused on the necessity of developing a checklist and internal documents for conducting independent oversight over intelligence and security institutions and the specifics that the oversight by the Ombudsperson entails. Participants discussed expectations for these documents, explored potential content and structure, and outlined next steps for creating practical oversight tool.

title.narrative: Indicator #2.3.1: Shielded Room and protected workspace constructed in Parliament and equipment installed.

comment.narrative: The Parliament has no protected workspace and meeting facility to discuss, and store classified information, impeding meaningful exchange of sensitive and classified information with security and intelligence services. Parliament, in Feb 2020, approved the establishment of the shielded room. Within its Phase I Programme DCAF allocated funds as a contribution towards the establishment of the Shielded Room and protected workplace. Due to Covid-19 the process was delayed throughout 2020.
By the end of 2021 the Parliament has a Shielded Room and protected space Installed.

As a result of the successful collaboration between DCAF and the Parliament of North Macedonia, the Shielded Room and Protected Workplace in the Parliament is officially open. On this occasion, a Ceremonial Opening took place in the Parliament on 21 October 2024. Designed to meet the highest security NATO and EU standards with most up-to-date equipment and cutting-edge technology, the Shielded Room ensures a secure environment for handling sensitive information. The facility reinforces the integrity of legislative processes by upholding confidentiality and accountability, while fostering a culture of security and trust. DCAF is grateful to the Parliament for their leadership and collaboration, as well as its commitment to democratic accountability, data integrity, and protection of sensitive information.

title.narrative: Indicator #2.6.1: A system for accountability in the use of intrusive methods (SIM), where different actors involved are aware of each other’s role and function in complementarity (judiciary, parliamentary committees, law enforcement, CCS, etc) is developed.
Guideline on Retention and Destruction of Data Collected by SIMs

comment.narrative: Weak inter-institutional strands such as: Criminal justice chain: police-prosecutors-judges; Judiciary-OTA – on ex-post judicial control, digitalization of warrants; Judiciary-Directorate for Personal Data Protection (DPDP)-Directorate for Security of Classified (DSCI) Information; Evaluation of the established procedures/standards for using, managing, handling, storing/keeping personal data and classified info by the judiciary; Judiciary-Parliament-CCS; Lack of material-technical resources that are required for the use of SIM within the MoI e.g. non-existence of proper facilities and equipment for listening and transcription of communications, thus failing to ensure the secrecy and protection of human rights.

By the end of 2023 most judicial practitioners working on criminal investigative matters have theoretical and practical knowledge on procedures and European standards for managing personal data and classified information.

During DCAF's activities and discussions with members of the judiciary, several practical challenges in implementing Special Investigative Measures (SIMs) were identified, primarily due to legislative inconsistencies. To address these challenges, DCAF hosted its second workshop with the judiciary group in Gevgelija from 20 to 22 November 2024. This workshop focused on reviewing current amendments and developing new proposals for the Law on Criminal Procedure, specifically regarding SIMs. The group, which includes members from the Ministry of Justice's official Working Group, is dedicated to addressing legislative gaps to ensure a modern, European-standard criminal procedure that upholds human rights while enhancing efficiency. This initiative seeks to align North Macedonia's criminal procedures with Euro-Atlantic standards, particularly in areas such as privacy, data retention, judicial oversight, proportionality, transparency, and accountability in the use of Special Investigative Measures (SIMs).

By the end of 2023 most judicial practitioners working on criminal investigative matters have theoretical and practical knowledge on procedures and European standards for managing personal data and classified information.

The final roundtable discussion and launch of the Guideline on Retention and Destruction of Data Collected by SIMs took place in Skopje on December 16. The newly developed guide systematizes and outlines procedures for storing and destroying data collected through Special Investigative Measures (SIMs). It incorporates international standards for data retention and destruction, addresses the challenges, obstacles, and limitations that may hinder the process, and specifies the individuals or entities responsible for the destruction process, along with their roles, duties, and responsibilities. This guideline was created at the request of the Basic Criminal Court – Skopje, in line with recommendations from the Agency for the Protection of Personal Data, following their supervisory work in the area of communications monitoring. The guide was developed through a series of workshops organized from June 2023 to October 2024, as part of the Intelligence and Security Sector Reform Program in the Republic of North Macedonia, implemented by DCAF.
